'''Troy Daniels''' (born July 15, 1991) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Virginia Commonwealth University]] (VCU), where in 2013, he set the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] record for made [[three-point field goals]] in a single game.

==High school career==
Daniels attended [[William Fleming High School]] in [[Roanoke, Virginia]]. As a senior in 2008–09, he was named Northwest Region Player of the Year and the [[Roanoke Times]] Player of the Year after averaging 17 points and six rebounds per game. He also earned Virginia High School Coaches' Association AAA First-Team All-State honors. He played in three straight VHSL AAA State Tournaments, including two appearances in the championship game in 2007 and 2009.<ref name=bio>{{cite web | title = #30 – Troy Daniels | work = vcuathletics.com | url = http://www.vcuathletics.com/sports/mbkb/2012-13/bios/daniels%20troy%20lghf | access-date = December 8, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==
As a collegiate player, Daniels played for [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] and under coach [[Shaka Smart]]. He played sparingly in his first two seasons for the Rams, though he did appear briefly in VCU's [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2011 Final Four]] game against [[2010–11 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] as a sophomore. As a junior in [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12]], Daniels became a regular in VCU's "Havoc" attack, averaging 24.4 minutes and 10 [[points per game]].<ref name="bio" />

As a senior in [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]], Daniels started every game and raised his scoring average to 12.3 points per game. He put his name in the record books on January 2, 2013, when he shot 11-of-20 from three-point range en route to 33 points and 10 rebounds in a 109–58 win over [[2012–13 East Tennessee State Buccaneers basketball team|East Tennessee State]]. The eleven three-pointers were a VCU and Atlantic 10 record for a single game.<ref>{{cite web | last = Brennan| first = Eamonn| title =Someone cool down VCU's Troy Daniels | work = ESPN.com | date = January 3, 2013| url = https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/71523/someone-cool-down-vcus-troy-daniels | access-date = December 8, 2013}}</ref> He also set VCU's single season record for three-pointers with 124,<ref name=BOBCAT>{{cite web | title = Troy Daniels signs with Charlotte Bobcats | work = RVANews.com | date = June 28, 2013 | url = http://rvanews.com/sports/troy-daniels-signs-with-charlotte-bobcats | access-date = December 8, 2013}}</ref> and finished with 251 three-pointers in his collegiate career, which ranked second most in the program's history.<ref>{{cite web | title = 2013 seniors: Troy Daniels, the human 9–0 run | work = RVANews.com | date = April 11, 2013 | url = http://rvanews.com/features/2013-seniors-troy-daniels-the-human-9-0-run/90061 | access-date = February 21, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2013–2014)===
After going undrafted in the [[2013 NBA draft]], Daniels joined the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].<ref name=BOBCAT/><ref>[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/charlotte-bobcats-announce-roster-2013-nba-summer-league-las-vegas Charlotte Bobcats Announce Roster for 2013 NBA Summer League in Las Vegas] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130712103515/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/charlotte-bobcats-announce-roster-2013-nba-summer-league-las-vegas |date=2013-07-12 }}</ref> On September 30, he signed with the Bobcats,<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14382 Bobcats add Troy Daniels, Abdul Gaddy, Patrick O’Bryant to training camp]</ref> but was later waived on October 10.<ref>[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/10/bobcats-release-daniels.html Bobcats Release Abdul Gaddy, Troy Daniels]</ref> On October 18, he signed with the [[Houston Rockets]],<ref>[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/10/rockets-sign-daniels.html Rockets Sign Troy Daniels]</ref> but was waived again on October 26.<ref>[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/10/rockets-waive-daniels.html Rockets Waive Troy Daniels]</ref> In November 2013, he was acquired by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Rockets. On January 4, 2014, against the [[Idaho Stampede]], Daniels made 10 three-pointers to go along with 32 points. Halfway through his first season with the Vipers, Daniels broke the D-League's single-season record in three-pointers made.<ref>{{cite web|title = Troy Daniels' Season Timeline: From NBA D-League to NBA Playoff Hero|url = http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/troy_daniels_houston_rockets_nba_dleague_rgv_vipers_timeline_2014_04_26.html|work = NBA.com|date = April 26, 2014|access-date = January 26, 2016|url-status = dead|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160329075214/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/troy_daniels_houston_rockets_nba_dleague_rgv_vipers_timeline_2014_04_26.html|archive-date = March 29, 2016}}</ref> On February 3, Daniels was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |date=2014-02-07 }}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2014)===
On February 21, 2014, Daniels signed with the [[Houston Rockets]] but was immediately assigned back to the Vipers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-troy-daniels-rgv-vipers Rockets Sign Troy Daniels From RGV Vipers]</ref><ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/troy_daniels_signs_rockets_rgv_vipers_callup_breakdown_2014_02_21.html Troy Daniels Signs with Houston Rockets: Call-Up Breakdown] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309103117/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/troy_daniels_signs_rockets_rgv_vipers_callup_breakdown_2014_02_21.html |date=2014-03-09 }}</ref> On March 3, he was recalled by the Rockets,<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4746561 Rockets Recall Daniels from the Vipers]</ref> and two days later, he made his NBA debut, playing a total of 92 seconds against the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20140305/HOUORL/gameinfo.html Notebook: Rockets 101, Magic 89]</ref> He was later reassigned to the Vipers two more times.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html 2013–14 NBA Assignments]</ref> In 50 games for the Vipers in 2013–14, he averaged 21.8 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.1 steals per game.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/d/danietr01d.html Troy Daniels D-League Stats]</ref>

On April 25, Daniels hit a go-ahead three-point shot with 11.0 seconds remaining in overtime against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in Game 3 of their [[2014 NBA Playoffs]] first-round match-up, which the Rockets won 121–116.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QYsK2Ost6Tg Troy Daniels Drains the Game-Winning 3-Pointer to Win Game 3!]</ref> Daniels finished the game with 17 points.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20140425/HOUPOR/gameinfo.html Notebook: Rockets 121, Blazers 116 OT]</ref><ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/troy_daniels_houston_rockets_nba_dleague_rgv_vipers_timeline_2014_04_26.html Troy Daniels' Season Timeline: From NBA D-League to NBA Playoff Hero] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429171636/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/troy_daniels_houston_rockets_nba_dleague_rgv_vipers_timeline_2014_04_26.html |date=2014-04-29 }}</ref> However, the Rockets went on to lose the series 4–2.

On July 14, 2014, Daniels re-signed with the Rockets.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-re-sign-troy-daniels Rockets Re-Sign Troy Daniels]</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2014–2015)===
On December 19, 2014, Daniels was acquired by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in a three-team trade that also involved the Rockets and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-troy-daniels-and-two-second-round-picks-houston Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Troy Daniels and Two Second-Round Picks from Houston]</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2015–2016)===
On February 10, 2015, Daniels was traded, along with [[Mo Williams]] and cash considerations, to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Gary Neal]] and a 2019 second-round draft pick.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-guards-mo-williams-troy-daniels-minnesota Hornets Acquire Guards Mo Williams, Troy Daniels from Minnesota]</ref> In the Hornets' final game of the season on April 15, Daniels scored a then career-high 24 points in a loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20150415/CHATOR/gameinfo.html Kyle Lowry leads Raptors to record 49th win]</ref>

On June 30, 2015, Daniels joined the Hornets for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-announce-2015-orlando-pro-summer-league-roster Hornets Announce 2015 Orlando Pro Summer League Roster]</ref> On January 22, 2016, he scored a then season-high 17 points in a 120–116 overtime win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160122/CHAORL/gameinfo.html Walker leads Hornets to 120–116 OT win over Magic]</ref> Three days later, he scored a career-high 28 points off the bench in a 129–128 double overtime win over the [[Sacramento Kings]]. In that game, he made eight three-pointers and hit the go-ahead three-pointer with nine seconds left in the second overtime period.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160125/CHASAC/gameinfo.html Cousins scores 56, sets Sacramento record in double-OT loss]</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VScF_OTjbpo Troy Daniels Nails 8 Three's, Including the Game Winner]</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2016–2017)===
On July 12, 2016, Daniels was acquired by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a sign-and-trade deal with the Charlotte Hornets.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/troy-daniels-acquired-160712 Grizzlies acquire Troy Daniels from Charlotte Hornets in sign-and-trade deal]</ref> On December 3, 2016, he scored a career-high 31 points in a 103–100 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He shot 12-of-23 from the field, including 6-of-12 from outside the arc.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899737 Daniels scores career-best 31 to lead Grizzlies past Lakers]</ref> Two days later, he hit seven three-pointers and finished with a game-high 29 points in a 110–108 double overtime win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899752|title=Gasol, Grizzlies outlast Pelicans, 110–108 in double OT|work=ESPN.com|date=December 5, 2016|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref> On December 29, he scored all 22 of his points in the fourth quarter of the Grizzlies' 114–80 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. Daniels' 22 points in the fourth tied a franchise record for one quarter—[[Greg Anthony]] had 22 in a quarter in December 1995, back when the team was in Vancouver.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899929|title=Gasol, Randolph lead Grizzlies past OKC as Westbrook tossed|work=ESPN.com|date=December 29, 2016|access-date=December 29, 2016}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2017–2019)===
On September 22, 2017, Daniels was traded, along with a 2018 second-round pick, to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for a conditional Suns 2018 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-acquire-troy-daniels-memphis|title=Suns Acquire Troy Daniels From Memphis|work=NBA.com|date=September 22, 2017|access-date=September 22, 2017}}</ref> On November 16, 2017, he scored 23 points, including six 3-pointers in the second quarter, in a 142–116 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974967|title=Harden, Rockets get 90 in first half, beat Suns 142–116|work=ESPN.com|date=November 16, 2017|access-date=November 16, 2017}}</ref> He tied a Suns franchise record for 3-pointers in a quarter, matching a mark shared by [[Gerald Green]] (in March 2014) and [[Shannon Brown]] (in November 2012).<ref>{{cite web|author=Phoenix Suns Stats|url=https://twitter.com/SunsBballComm/status/931381426351611904|title=Troy Daniels has tied a @Suns franchise...|work=Twitter|date=November 16, 2017|access-date=November 16, 2017}}</ref> On December 13, 2017, Daniels scored a career-high 32 points on 11-of-16 shooting, including 7-of-10 on 3-pointers, in a 115–109 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975162|title=Demar DeRozan has 37 points, Raptors beat Suns 115–109|work=ESPN.com|date=December 13, 2017|access-date=December 14, 2017}}</ref> On January 22, 2018, in a 109–105 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400975437|title=Suns vs. Bucks – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=January 22, 2018|access-date=January 24, 2018}}</ref> Daniels made a three-pointer off the bench in his 27th straight game, passing [[Wesley Person]] for the longest such streak in Suns franchise history.<ref>{{cite web|author=Phoenix Suns Stats|url=https://twitter.com/SunsBballComm/status/955633385635901441|title=Troy Daniels has now made a three-pointer...|work=Twitter|date=January 22, 2018|access-date=January 24, 2018}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2019–2020)===
On July 7, 2019, Daniels signed a one-year contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for $2.1 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/190707-lakers-sign-daniels-dudley|title=Lakers Sign Troy Daniels and Jared Dudley|website=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> On March 1, 2020, Daniels was waived by the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers waive Troy Daniels|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/03/01/troy-daniels-lakers-waive|date=March 1, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 1, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Maloney |first1=Jack |title=Lakers waive Troy Daniels to create open roster spot, but have no imminent plans to sign anyone, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/lakers-waive-troy-daniels-to-create-open-roster-spot-but-have-no-imminent-plans-to-sign-anyone-per-report/ |access-date=March 1, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 1, 2020}}</ref> The Lakers later won the [[2020 NBA Finals]] and sent Daniels an [[NBA championship ring]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Mark|last=Berman|title=Former Roanoker and NBA veteran Troy Daniels looking forward to playing in Italy|date=July 29, 2021|newspaper=The Roanoke Times|url=https://roanoke.com/sports/high-school/former-roanoker-and-nba-veteran-troy-daniels-looking-forward-to-playing-in-italy/article_740a3bd2-f095-11eb-96d9-77c1b3420a3d.html|access-date=August 20, 2021}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2020)===
On March 5, 2020, Daniels signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nugs-troy-daniels-20200305a|title=Denver Nuggets sign Troy Daniels|date=March 5, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 5, 2020}}</ref>

===Olimpia Milano (2021–2022)===
On July 12, 2021, Daniels moved to Europe after signing a one-year deal with [[EuroLeague]] team [[Olimpia Milano]], under coach [[Ettore Messina]].<ref>{{cite web |title="I want to embrace the culture and the fans, I feel fortunate": Troy Daniels is coming to Milano |url=http://www.olimpiamilano.com/en/i-want-to-embrace-the-culture-and-the-fans-i-feel-fortunate-troy-daniels-is-coming-to-milano/ |website=olimpiamilano.com |date=12 July 2021 |language=Italian }}</ref> On June 27, 2022, he parted ways with the Italian club.
